 Order

1. The appellants are before this Court calling in question an order dated 13.04.2023 passed by the learned Sessions Judge declining to grant the petitioners/accused Nos.2, 3 and 4 anticipatory bail in Crime No.143/2022 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 355, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 (hereinafter referred to as 'the SC/ST Act').
2. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants.
3. Briefs facts that leads the appellants to this Court are as follows:

sentences.text: The 2nd respondent is the complainant, wife of accused No.1 who is not before the Court.
The petitioner No.1 is accused No.2, wife of accused No.1.
Petitioner No.2 is the sister of accused No.1.
Petitioner No.3 is the brother of accused No.1.

All the petitioners are hauled into the web of the crime for the aforesaid offences on the ground that the husband along with the petitioners have indulged in certain acts which would become punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 355, 504 and 506 of IPC as well as Sections 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

4. On registration of the crime, the petitioners herein knocked at the door of the learned Sessions Judge in Criminal Misc.No.272/2023 by which the learned Sessions Judge declined to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioners on the ground that there a bar to grant pre- arrest bail to the accused if the offences are punishable under the Act.
It is therefore the petitioners have knocked at the doors of this Court in the subject petition.

5. The learned counsel for the petitioners seek to place reliance upon the judgment of the Co-ordinate Bench which declines to accept the bar under the Act to grant anticipatory bail and submits that the offences against the petitioners are neither punishable with imprisonment for life nor death penalty.
It is a family dispute.
6. The learned HCGP would however refute the submission to contend that the bail to the petitioners should not be granted as they have indulged in offences which are punishable under the Act.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the respective submissions and have perused the material on record.
8. The afore-narrated facts are not in dispute.
The complainant is the 1st wife of accused No.1.
The petitioners are the alleged 2nd wife and the brother and sister of accused No.1.
Therefore the dispute is between the members of the family.

The offences alleged are under Sections 498A, 323, 355, 504 and 506 of IPC and the provisions of the Act on the ground that the accused No.1- hsuband and other members of the family hurled abuses on the 2nd respondent-complainant.
All these are a matter of evidence which will have to be thrashed out in a full blown trial.
The offences are neither punishable with life or death penalty.
Charge-sheet has also been filed and therefore the petitioners would not be required for any further investigation/interrogation.

For the aforesaid reasons, I pass the following:
ORDER 1.
The criminal appeal filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. is allowed.

2. The petitioners/accused Nos.2, 3 and 4 by name (1) Priyanka W/o.Manjunath Mulimani, (2) Rajamma W/o.Sharanappa Karthik, (3) Rajappa S/o. Shamanna Mulimani, all are residents of Tawargera, Kushtagi taluk, Koppal district are ordered Priyanka W/O Manjunath Mulimani vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177797769/
3 to be enlarged on bail in the event of their arrest in Crime No.143/2022 of Tawargera P.S., registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 355, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 3(1)(r), 3(1)(s) of the SC/ST Act subject to the following conditions:
i. The petitioners/accused Nos.2, 3 and 4 shall execute a self bond for Rs.50,000/-
each with one surety for the like sum, to the satisfaction of the investigating officer or SHO of Tawargera PS.
ii. The petitioners shall not try to tamper the prosecution witnesses directly or indirectly.

iii. The petitioners shall appear before the concerned SHO or Investigating Officer within ten days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order and co-operate with the investigation of the case.

On completion of interrogation, the petitioners shall be released on bail by the SHO or Investigating Officer of concerned Police Station forthwith on the terms and conditions mentioned in this order.

iv. The petitioners shall mark their attendance before the SHO of Tawargera Police Station on every alternative Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 4.00 p.m. for a period of three months or till filing of charge sheet whichever is earlier.

v.
The petitioners shall furnish authenticated documents in proof of their residential and correct address and shall inform the Court/Police if there is any change in the address and furnish their mobile phone number/numbers to Court and I.O. vi.
The petitioners shall not involve in any criminal activities and shall not commit similar offences.
vii. The petitioners shall appear before the Court during trial of case if any on all dates of hearing without fail unless their presence is dispensed.
In case if any of the condition is violated, the prosecution is at liberty to move application for cancellation of bail.
